correctness.rationale: The cut-indicator proof reconstructs. With positive adjacent gaps, centered scores are positive combinations of nested upper-cut indicators H_j. Their covariance is P_min(1-P_max), and the normalized cut correlation is minimized by j=1,k=m-1, giving squared floor p1*pm/((1-p1)(1-pm)). Positivity plus the L2 triangle inequality transfers this floor to arbitrary strict codings; diagonal terms make it strict for m>=3. Dominant first-versus-last gap sequences approach the floor, Cauchy--Schwarz gives correlation at most one with equality exactly for positive affine recodings, and connectedness gives the entire interval. An independent random-gap stress test for m=3,...,7 approached but never crossed the bound.
